title: Electromagnetic Wave Propagation (E/B Vector Field Visualization)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a visualization of an electromagnetic wave propagating along the +Z axis: represent the electric field E and magnetic field B with arrows (ArrowHelper or custom arrows), demonstrating plane-wave, circular-polarization, and elliptical-polarization behavior in which E⊥B and the fields are in phase.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Fields and Geometry]
(1) The propagation direction is +Z. Uniformly place 50 sampling points along the Z axis to draw E-field arrows and 50 sampling points to draw B-field arrows. Their Z positions may be offset, or they may share the same Z positions and be distinguished by color, but the concept of two clearly visible groups totaling 100 arrows must be preserved: 50 E + 50 B.
(2) E oscillates in the XZ plane, with its primary component along X varying with Z and t; B oscillates in the YZ plane, with its primary component along Y. They must satisfy E⊥B and both must be perpendicular to the propagation direction.
(3) Linear polarization: E_x = E0 cos(kz - ωt), and B_y is in phase with E_x. Under the vacuum approximation, it is sufficient for their amplitude relationship to be consistent. For circular/elliptical polarization, combine two orthogonal components in the plane perpendicular to Z, with an adjustable phase difference.
(4) Wave parameters: k = 2π/λ and ω = 2πf. Use the λ and f sliders to control the visual wavelength and oscillation frequency.

[Interactive Controls]
(5) Wavelength slider id="wavelength", range 1–10, step 0.1 or 0.5, default approximately 4.
(6) Frequency slider id="frequency", range 0.5–5, step 0.1, default 1.
(7) Polarization mode: a dropdown or button group with id="polarization" and values including at least linear, circular, and elliptical; the value of a <select> may be used.
(8) Show/hide the B field: a checkbox or switch with id="showB"; checked means visible.

[Animation and Rendering]
(9) Update the arrow directions and lengths every frame based on simTime. A uniform length scale may be used to represent the amplitude envelope.
(10) Use a dark background, grid or axis helpers, and OrbitControls.
(11) Optional: illustrative wavefront lines or translucent planes; these are not required.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - wavelength: number
  - frequency: number
  - polarization: string ('linear'|'circular'|'elliptical')
  - showB: boolean
  - simTime: number (seconds)
  - maxAmplitudeE: number
  - maxAmplitudeB: number

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
